title: Turn Down the Night
bodyMd:
This is an argumentative passage. Three portions are marked with a bracketed number and shown in **bold**. Each question names the portion it asks about.

**Paragraph 1.** Our county council will vote next month on whether to replace every streetlight with a shielded, warm-white fixture that throws its light downward. The proposal is usually described as an astronomy measure, and a shielded lamp does give stargazers back a piece of the sky. The strongest reasons to vote yes, though, have nothing to do with telescopes.

**Paragraph 2.** Start with money. A shielded fixture aims its output at the pavement, so a lower-wattage lamp does the same work. The twelve fixtures replaced last year on Mill Street draw about forty percent less power than the lamps they replaced, and the county paid nothing for the poles it already owned.

**Paragraph 3.** Then consider what the current lamps do to everything that is awake at night. **[1] Circling until dawn, the glare from an unshielded lamp keeps moths from the flowers they should be pollinating.** Birds that migrate by starlight are pulled off course by the same upward spill.

**Paragraph 4.** **[2] Therefore,** the objection that matters is safety: will a dimmer street be a more dangerous one? The county’s night-time collision count on Mill Street did not rise after the retrofit. **[3] The list of complaints filed with the sheriff’s office in the twelve months after the change were** shorter than the list from the year before, and several residents wrote that they could finally see an oncoming car before its headlights cleared the glare.
accessibilityText: A four-paragraph argumentative passage urging a county council to vote for shielded, downward-facing streetlights, arguing from electricity cost and harm to night-active wildlife, then answering the safety objection with figures from a trial on Mill Street. Three spots are marked for editing. Marked spot one, in paragraph three, is the whole sentence "Circling until dawn, the glare from an unshielded lamp keeps moths from the flowers they should be pollinating." Marked spot two is the transition word "Therefore," at the start of paragraph four. Marked spot three, also in paragraph four, is the clause "The list of complaints filed with the sheriff’s office in the twelve months after the change were".

provenance.notes: Original passage. The county, Mill Street and all figures are invented for this item set; nothing is taken from a published ACT English passage.
